passages.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath.
His disciples were with Him.
The disciples began to pick heads of grain.
They rubbed the grain in their hands.
They ate the grain.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν

passages.text: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees saw Jesus and His disciples.
These Pharisees spoke to them.
They asked a question.
They said, “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
passages.original: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He answered their question.
Jesus reminded them of a story about David.
David was hungry.
David’s companions were also hungry.
Jesus asked if they had read what David did at that time.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες

passages.text: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”
passages.sermon:
David was hungry.
His companions were also hungry.
David entered the house of God.
He took the consecrated bread.
He ate the consecrated bread.
He gave the consecrated bread to his companions.
Only priests are allowed to eat this bread.
David and his companions ate bread that only priests may eat.
passages.original: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς

passages.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Jesus called himself the Son of Man.
Jesus said he has authority over the Sabbath.
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath.
On another Sabbath, Jesus entered the synagogue.
Jesus was teaching in the synagogue.
A man was present in the synagogue.
The man’s right hand was withered.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά

passages.text: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
passages.sermon: The scribes and the Pharisees watched Jesus closely.\r\nThey wanted to find a reason to accuse Him.\r\nThey watched to see if Jesus would heal on the Sabbath.
passages.original: παρετηροῦντο δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the synagogue on the Sabbath.
Jesus was teaching.
A man was there.
The man’s right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees watched Jesus closely.
They wanted to accuse Jesus if He healed on the Sabbath.
Jesus knew the thoughts of the scribes and Pharisees.
Jesus spoke to the man with the withered hand.
Jesus said, “Get up and stand among us.”
The man got up.
The man stood there.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Is it lawful to do good on the Sabbath?”
He also said, “Or is it lawful to do evil on the Sabbath?”
He said, “Is it lawful to save a life on the Sabbath?”
He also said, “Or is it lawful to destroy a life on the Sabbath?”
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι

passages.text: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among the people in the synagogue.
He looked at everyone there.
He spoke to the man with the withered hand.
Jesus said, “Stretch out your hand.”
The man stretched out his hand.
His hand became healthy again.
passages.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.
passages.sermon: The scribes and Pharisees became very angry.\r\nThey talked to each other.\r\nThey discussed what they might do to Jesus.
passages.original: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
In those days, Jesus went out to a mountain.
He went there to pray.
Jesus prayed to God.
He stayed all night in prayer.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot; Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was the Son of God.
He had many disciples.
When daylight came, Jesus called His disciples to Him.
He chose twelve men from among them.
He called these twelve men apostles.
Their names were Simon, whom Jesus named Peter, and Andrew, Peter’s brother.
James and John were also chosen.
Philip and Bartholomew were chosen.
Matthew and Thomas were chosen.
James, the son of Alphaeus, was chosen.
Simon, who was called the Zealot, was chosen.
Judas, the son of James, was chosen.
Judas Iscariot was also chosen.
Judas Iscariot later became a traitor.
passages.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης

passages.text: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus chose twelve apostles from among His disciples.
Jesus came down from the mountain with His apostles.
Jesus stood on a level place.
A large crowd of Jesus’ disciples was present.
Many other people were also there.
These people came from all over Judea.
Some people came from Jerusalem.
Some people came from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.
passages.original: Καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος

passages.text: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
passages.sermon:
Many people came to Jesus.
They wanted to hear Jesus speak.
They wanted Jesus to heal their diseases.
Some people had unclean spirits.
Jesus healed those troubled by unclean spirits.
passages.original: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο

passages.text: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among a large crowd.
The entire crowd tried to touch Jesus.
Power came out from Jesus.
This power healed everyone.
passages.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ ὅτι δύναμις παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας

passages.text: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
He looked up at them.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Blessed are you who are poor.
The kingdom of God belongs to you.”
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί Ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Blessed are you who are hungry now.
God will fill you.
Blessed are you who weep now.
God will make you laugh.”
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν Ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε Μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν Ὅτι γελάσετε

passages.text: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Blessed are you when people hate you.
Blessed are you when people exclude you.
Blessed are you when people insult you.
Blessed are you when people reject your name as evil.
They do these things because of the Son of Man.”
passages.original: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He tells them about suffering for his sake.
He says, "Rejoice in that day."
He says, "Leap for joy."
He explains the reason.
He says, "Your reward is great in heaven."
He gives an example from history.
He says, "Their fathers treated the prophets the same way."
passages.original: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν

passages.text: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
He warns the rich.
He says, “Woe to you who are rich.”
You have already received your comfort.
You will not receive more comfort from God.
passages.original: Πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις Ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν

passages.text: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
He warns those who are well fed now.
He says, "Woe to you who are well fed now."
You will become hungry.
He warns those who laugh now.
He says, "Woe to you who laugh now."
You will mourn.
You will weep.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν Ὅτι πεινάσετε Οὐαί οἱ γελῶντες νῦν Ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε

passages.text: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He warns about seeking praise from people.
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you.
People once praised the false prophets in the same way.
Their ancestors treated false prophets with honor.
Receiving praise from everyone can be a sign of falsehood.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι Κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν

passages.text: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to those who are willing to listen.
He says, love your enemies.
Do good to people who hate you.
Bless people who curse you.
Pray for people who mistreat you.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν Ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς

passages.text: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his followers.
He teaches them how to respond to mistreatment.
If a person strikes you on one cheek, offer the other cheek also.
If a person takes your cloak, do not stop him from taking your tunic too.
passages.original: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς

passages.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his followers.
He teaches them how to treat others.
Give to everyone who asks you.
If anyone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back.
passages.original: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει

passages.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches his followers how to treat other people.
He says, “Do to others as you would have them do to you.”
Treat people the way you want them to treat you.
Show kindness and fairness to everyone.
Let your actions toward others match how you hope they will act toward you.
This is a clear rule for living among others.
passages.original: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως

passages.text: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches about love.
If you love only people who love you, you gain nothing special.
Sinners also love people who love them.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν

passages.text: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches about true goodness.
If you do good to people who do good to you, you gain no special credit.
Sinners also do good to those who do good to them.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν

passages.text: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches about true love and generosity.
If you lend to people who will pay you back, you gain nothing special.
Sinners also lend to other sinners.
They expect to receive back the same amount.
There is no special credit in this.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ’ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα

passages.text: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
passages.sermon:
God is the Most High.
God is kind to ungrateful people.
God is kind to wicked people.
You must love your enemies.
You must do good to your enemies.
You must lend to your enemies.
Do not expect anything back when you lend.
If you do these things, your reward will be great.
If you do these things, you will be sons of the Most High.
passages.original: Πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς

passages.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God is merciful.
You must be merciful.
Be merciful as your Father is merciful.
passages.original: Γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καθὼς καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν

passages.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them how to treat others.
Do not judge other people.
If you do not judge, others will not judge you.
Do not condemn other people.
If you do not condemn, others will not condemn you.
Forgive other people.
If you forgive, you will be forgiven.
passages.original: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε ἀπολύετε καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε

passages.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about giving.
He said, “Give to others.
God will give to you.
God will give you a good measure.
This measure will be pressed down.
It will be shaken together.
It will be running over.
God will pour this into your lap.
The measure you use for others is important.
God will use the same measure for you.”
passages.original: δίδοτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
He said, “Can a blind man lead another blind man?
Both men are blind.
If one blind man leads another, both will fall into a pit.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ἐμπεσοῦνται

passages.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
passages.sermon: A disciple is a student who learns from a teacher.\r\nA disciple is not greater than his teacher.\r\nWhen a disciple is fully trained, he will be like his teacher.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, "Why do you look at the small speck in your brother’s eye?
You do not notice the large beam in your own eye."
He pointed out their failure to see their own greater faults.
He showed that people often judge others while ignoring their own problems.
passages.original: Τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς

passages.text: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about judging others.
You may see a small speck in your brother’s eye.
You may want to remove it.
But you have a large beam in your own eye.
You do not notice your own fault.
You say, “Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye.”
But you do not see the beam in your own eye.
You are a hypocrite.
First, take the beam out of your own eye.
Then you will see clearly.
Then you can remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
passages.original: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἀδελφέ ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων ὑποκριτά ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν

passages.text: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
passages.sermon: A good tree does not bear bad fruit.\r\nA bad tree does not bear good fruit.
passages.original: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν

passages.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.
passages.sermon: Each tree is recognized by its own fruit.\r\nPeople do not pick figs from thornbushes.\r\nPeople do not gather grapes from brambles.
passages.original: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν

passages.text: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.
passages.sermon:
A good man has a good heart.
He keeps good treasure in his heart.
He brings out good things from this treasure.
An evil man has an evil heart.
He keeps evil treasure in his heart.
He brings out evil things from this treasure.
The mouth speaks what fills the heart.
Words show what is inside the heart.
passages.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord’?
You do not do what I say.”
passages.original: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε Κύριε κύριε καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω

passages.text: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He described a person who comes to Him.
This person hears the words of Jesus.
This person does what Jesus says.
Jesus explained what this person is like.
He is like a man who builds a house.
The man digs deep.
He lays the foundation on solid rock.
A flood comes.
A river crashes against the house.
The house does not fall.
The water cannot shake the house.
The house stands strong because it is well built.
passages.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν

passages.text: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus described two kinds of people.
One person hears the words of Jesus but does not do them.
This person is like a man.
The man builds a house.
He builds the house on the ground.
He does not lay a foundation.
A flood comes.
The river crashes against the house.
The house falls down at once.
The destruction of that house is great.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα
